simple.meaning: זְמַן (zᵉman) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to agree (on a time and place).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:9. The surrounding contexts include Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זְמַן (H2164) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זְמַן (zᵉman) / H2164 is traced through Daniel 2:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: But if you don’t make known to me the dream, there is but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the situation changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can show me its interpretation.”

definitions.full: H2164. zeman [ זְמַן ] verb denominative Hithpa`el agree together ( ᵑ7 ); — Perfect 3masculine plural Dan 2:9 Qr הִזְדַּמִּנְתּוּן (D 211, 2nd ed. 263 M § 12 a ; Kt Haph`el הַזְמִנְתּוּן , see ᵑ7 Onk Exod 5:14 D (2) 263, 403), followed by Infinitive לְמֵאמַר .
